StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single with the sim's on_stack overridden to `pass` citing it -- the settled census's 15-unit wrong-reasoning class (`py tools/audit/power_census.py stack`). Single means "Amount is hidden and is always 1" (PowerStackType.cs:10-13); PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236) adds unconditionally with no StackType branch, so C# really reaches Amount 2. Dormant: nothing reads Adaptable's Amount on either side -- the revive machinery is driven by the private `isReviving` / `is_reviving` flag (AdaptablePower.cs:13, powers.py:3360) -- and monsters/glory/test_subject.py applies it once at combat start. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.issue: THE HOOK IS THE WRONG ONE, and the consequences are observable. C# lets the death HAPPEN: Hook.ShouldDie returns true, CreatureCmd.cs:507-508 fires InvokeDiedEvent and computes shouldRemoveFromCombat = false (from this power's ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath), then AfterDeath sets isReviving and calls TestSubject.TriggerDeadState() -- leaving the Test Subject **dead at 0 HP, retained in combat**, with the combat held open by ShouldStopCombatFromEnding. The sim instead PREVENTS the death from `should_die` (powers.py:3365-3370 returns False), and cmds.py:106-113 then floors the creature at **1 HP** and leaves `is_dead` False. Three observable consequences. (1) HP: 1 vs 0, which conformance asserts on directly. (2) damage_pipeline gap G4 -- C# locks the AfterDamageReceived-skip decision to the pre-Kill snapshot so an arithmetically lethal hit permanently skips the victim's on-damage-received powers, while the sim resets HP to 1 first and only then tests `target.is_dead` (cmds.py:121), so the Test Subject's Enrage and every other on_damage_received listener fires in the sim and not in the game. Not re-verdicted (rule 3). (3) Feed: `Feed.cs:38` computes `shouldTriggerFatal = cardPlay.Target.Powers.All(p => p.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal())` and AdaptablePower does NOT override it (default true), and `WasTargetKilled` is true, so **the game grants the +3 max HP for Feeding the Test Subject to death**; the sim's `if target.is_dead` (cards/feed.py:45) is False, so it grants nothing -- and the sim's own docstring (cards/feed.py:17-18) asserts the opposite behaviour is correct. EXECUTED (sim side): after a lethal Strike the Test Subject sits at hp 1 with `is_dead` False. LIVE: Feed is a ported Rare Ironclad Attack and the Test Subject is the ported Act-3 Glory boss. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldAllowHitting.issue: LIVE, and it upgrades a seam gap that was recorded as un-demonstrated. C#'s PowerCmd.Apply<T> refuses to apply anything to a creature `CanReceivePowers` says no to, and CanReceivePowers reuses Hook.ShouldAllowHitting -- which is exactly what this override's own doc comment says it is for ("This is so the ... doesn't receive POWERS while it is reviving"). The sim wires should_allow_hitting into DamageCmd.deal (cmds.py:51-52) but NOT into PowerCmd.apply, which has no such guard at all. That is `power_cmd` gap **G6**, whose text says "No concrete broken interaction is demonstrated (spot-checked callers apply powers only to already-resolved targets)". **That is now falsified. EXECUTED:** a TEST_SUBJECT_BOSS combat (the Test Subject starts with powers ['adaptable', 'enrage']), a lethal Strike, then Vulnerable 2 from the player -- the sim reports `is_reviving True`, `should_allow_hitting(ts) False`, and then still lands `Vulnerable(2)` on the reviving boss, where the game refuses the application outright. Control: a 10-damage Strike in the same window returns 0 HP lost, proving the predicate IS wired into the damage path and only the power path is missing it. Rule-6 co-occurrence: the Test Subject is the ported Act-3 Glory boss and applies this power to itself at combat start, Bash/Vulnerable is ported basic-pool Ironclad content, and the revive window is the remainder of the player's turn after the killing blow -- the ordinary flow of the fight, not a contrived state. The same override exists on IllusionPower and ReattachPower, so all three carry it. Verdict carried per rule 3; the seam record is not edited (half B does not own audits/seam/** or docs/audit/seams/**) -- reported in .superpowers/sdd/content-power-report-b.md section 2.3. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldStopCombatFromEnding.issue: No sim counterpart. C# reads this through Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding at CombatManager.cs:196, i.e. inside the win check: while ANY power on ANY creature returns true the combat cannot end. The sim has no such hook -- `hooks.py` defines no `should_stop_combat_from_ending` -- and `combat.py:272-277` decides the win purely from `is_gone` over the non-minion enemies. The sim reaches the same OUTCOME by a different route in each case (see this record's death entry), but the mechanism is absent, so a future power that wants to hold combat open without also preventing a death or adding a creature has nothing to hook. Dormant: all five ported overrides (AdaptablePower, InfestedPower, SteamEruptionPower, StockPower, SurprisePower) are paired with either a death prevention or a mid-death spawn that keeps `_all_enemies_dead()` false on its own. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.maps_to: hooks.py:603 should_remove_from_combat_after_death -- NOT implemented by this power
ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.issue: The sim HAS the hook (hooks.py:603, consumed at cmds.py:102-104 to set `retained_after_death`) and this power does not use it, because the sim took the death-prevention route instead (see the AfterDeath entry). Folded into that entry's mechanism: in C# the Test Subject is a retained corpse and in the sim it is a live creature at 1 HP. Carried separately because it is the specific unused hook, and because ReattachPower one file over DOES implement it (powers.py:2338-2341) -- so the sim is inconsistent between two powers with the same C# shape.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath() => false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533 (`creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath()`, then each power's AfterRemoved) and this override opts out so the power survives the death it is supposed to react to. The sim never removes powers on death at all -- a grep of cmds.py's kill/death path finds no `powers.clear()` or per-power removal, and cmds.py:96-105 goes straight from the HP write to should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death -- so `false` is the sim's universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. Faithful HERE. The inverse is a real machinery gap owned by nobody: the C# DEFAULT is `true`, so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is. That is reported in content-power-report-b.md section 3 rather than verdicted on this unit, because it is an engine-wide absence and not this power's divergence. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
